question: Should existing GitHub-backed skills with over-40-character stored display names be grandfathered like hosted skills, or intentionally shortened on the next sync?
rationale: The PR makes a compatibility-sensitive stored catalog policy choice for GitHub-backed skills, and automation cannot infer whether maintainers want preservation or sync-time migration.

options.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed legacy names
options.body: Preserve unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names and enforce the new limit only for new or renamed GitHub-backed entries.

options.title: Accept sync-time shortening
options.body: Allow next sync to shorten existing over-limit GitHub-backed titles, but require explicit PR/issue documentation and real sync proof before merge.

options.title: Pause display-name policy
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers choose the public maximum length and legacy handling across hosted and GitHub-backed skills.

recommendation.title: Grandfather GitHub-backed legacy names
recommendation.body: Preserve unchanged existing over-limit GitHub-backed display names and enforce the new limit only for new or renamed GitHub-backed entries.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen has the strongest recent history on the GitHub-backed sync and shared publish paths affected by this policy.
